+    // oci_ref is the digest-pinned reference of a profile previously pulled

+    // It is the same string as image.image and image.user_specified_image
+    // of the PullSecurityProfile request, because the pod spec only allows
+    // canonical, digest-pinned references.
+    // The runtime uses it to look up the cached profile content and must

+    // Must be set if `ProfileType` is `OCI`; runtimes must ignore it for

+    string oci_ref = 3;
+    // base_profile specifies an optional base profile to merge with the OCI
+    // profile. Only meaningful if `ProfileType` is `OCI`; runtimes must
+    // ignore it for other profile types.
+    // The runtime intersects the OCI profile, the base profile, and its own
+    // configured baseline, so that the effective profile permits an
+    // operation only if all inputs permit it.
+    // The configured baseline is the runtime default profile unless the node
+    // administrator configured a different profile. A RuntimeDefault base
+    // profile therefore only adds restrictions on nodes with such a
+    // configuration.
+    // When unset, the runtime uses its configured baseline only.
+    SecurityProfileBase base_profile = 4;

+        BaseTypeUnspecified = 0;

discussion_comments.comment_body: I went with your last option: `RuntimeDefault = 0` and `Localhost = 1`, like `SecurityProfile.ProfileType`. A pod without a base profile still gets no `base_profile` message, because on nodes with a custom baseline, always sending `RuntimeDefault` would add restrictions the pod didn't ask for. The comment tells runtimes to check that the message is set, since its zero type now selects `RuntimeDefault`.
is this intentionally aligning the default / absent value with the current read-only behavior, or do we need to be able to distinguish unspecified from specified-and-0?

Yeah this is intentional. I think the default value should be the current read-only behavior, which looks also be the pattern we've used for other enums like `SupplementalGroupsPolicy`. I can't think of a case where we'd want to differentiate that it's unset
Revisiting this, actually I think we do need an `UNSPECIFIED` value, see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/139824#issuecomment-5689734546
